corpus.title: Palestinian Authority President Abbas postpones November legislative elections until late 2027
corpus.signal_text:
Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree on Saturday canceling legislative elections scheduled for November 28, 2026, and setting presidential and legislative elections for September 11, 2027, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
The new decree calls on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip to participate in "free and direct elections to elect the Palestinian president and members of the Palestinian Legislative Council simultaneously, in accordance with the law," WAFA said.
This follows consultations among Palestinian factions, political forces, and the Executive Committee of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO).
The Executive Committee reached a consensus, deciding that Israeli measures in the West Bank and Gaza posed a significant obstacle to holding elections at the previously scheduled date, WAFA explained, adding that the postponement is to allow for the establishment of "suitable political, security and field conditions for free, fair and inclusive elections."
WAFA cited Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence, restrictions on freedom of movement, and the withholding of Palestinian revenues.
PA vice president reportedly informed France of election postponement
The WAFA report follows Palestinian Vice President Hussein Al Sheikh informing France of election postponements, citing worsening conditions across the Palestinian territories, according to a Thursday-dated letter addressed to French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot seen by Reuters.
"The assessment concluded that the anticipated political, security and economic conditions, on which the scheduling of the legislative elections for November 28, 2026, was based, have not materialized," the letter said. "Holding them (the legislative elections) under the current circumstances faces fundamental obstacles affecting their inclusiveness, freedom of participation, and the integrity of the electoral process."

corpus.title: Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
corpus.signal_text:
Abbas postpones Palestinian elections, sets presidential poll for September 2027
RAMALLAH, Oct 10 - Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas on Saturday cancelled legislative elections scheduled for November due to worsening conditions within the Palestinian territories and set a date of September 11, 2027 for both presidential and legislative elections, the official Palestinian news agency WAFA reported.
Abbas' decree cited "obstacles posed by Israeli measures" to holding elections in November and the need to establish suitable political, security and on-the-ground conditions for "free, fair and inclusive elections". It called on Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza to participate in the polls.
There had been serious doubts that the Palestinian Authority vote would go ahead in late November. The Palestinians have not held legislative or presidential elections since 2005-06, after which Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas' rival, the Islamist group Hamas, seized control of Gaza, ousting his loyalists.
The decree said Israeli military attacks, settlement expansion, settler violence and movement restrictions in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, along with Israel's continued withholding of Palestinian tax revenues, created challenges to preparing for and holding elections on the previous date.
In Gaza, the decree pointed to "exceptional security and humanitarian conditions", the incomplete withdrawal of Israeli forces, the lack of progress in reconstruction and the failure to implement arrangements for deploying international stabilisation forces and police.
Israeli restrictions on access for election commission staff and international observers to Gaza and East Jerusalem also complicated preparations, the decree said.
The decision to postpone followed a resolution by the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee and consultations with Palestinian factions and political forces. It also aimed to allow time for a comprehensive Palestinian national dialogue to strengthen unity and address challenges facing the electoral process. REUTERS
